headline: OPENAI PROPOSES
A **SPEED LIMIT**
cover.hook_pick_reason: No reader-impact hook: the articles describe a proposal for AI labs to agree shared limits and state no effect on ordinary readers (their costs, tools or rights). The claim hook is the strongest the slides fully support: the OpenAI post proposes common limits developers commit not to cross, and every slide builds on it. It does not say anyone has agreed, since TechCrunch says only 'seemingly endorsed'. The number hook is accurate (about 0.91 for GPT-4, below 0.8 now) but a bare score means little without context. The quote hook rests on Altman's words as reported by TechCrunch but tells readers less about the idea.

slides.title: OpenAI wants labs to agree a speed limit
body: Jakub Pachocki, OpenAI's chief scientist, argues in a post that AI developers should agree **common limits** they commit not to cross. The post is called "Perplexity and Intelligence" and was published this weekend.

slides.title: The measure is called perplexity
body: Perplexity is a score of how well a model **predicts the next token** on average. Lower is better. Pachocki wants it used to compare model developers and inform shared safety standards.

slides.title: From 0.91 to below 0.8
body: OpenAI says GPT-4, at about **0.91**, was good at chain-of-thought reasoning. With losses now **below 0.8**, it has seen transformative capabilities emerge in cybersecurity and mathematics.

slides.title: No cap yet, and real hurdles
body: The limits would hold until our ability to understand and monitor AI reaches a **concrete milestone**. The post sets no number. OpenAI itself lists a challenge: comparing across labs, which use different datasets.

slides.title: Altman calls it a big one
body: Sam Altman called the post "the most important thing OpenAI has published in a while," TechCrunch reports. Anthropic's Dario Amodei published a plan to "pace the frontier," **seemingly endorsed** by Altman and Elon Musk.

facts.text: In this post, I argue for establishing perplexity (or, equivalently, cross-entropy loss) as a metric to compare between model developers and inform shared safety standards.
Perplexity measures how well a model predicts the next token on average; lower perplexity means better predictions.
GPT-4, at ~0.91, was proficient at utilizing chain-of-thought reasoning productively.
Now, as we have reached losses below 0.8, we have seen the emergence of transformative capabilities in fields like cybersecurity and mathematics.

I further propose common limits, based on perplexity and other measurements, that developers are committed to not crossing until our ability to understand and monitor AI behavior achieves a certain concrete milestone.
Perplexity as a shared metric has challenges: Difficulty of comparison across labs. Different developers use different evaluation datasets and train on different data mixtures.
By Jakub Pachocki, Chief Scientist at OpenAI. Published November 22, 2026.
Pachocki's post, described by Altman as "the most important thing OpenAI has published in a while", suggests perplexity could be that measurement.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei then published a plan to "pace the frontier," seemingly endorsed by OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk.

sources.title: OpenAI’s chief scientist has thoughts on how to limit AI development

caption:
OpenAI's chief scientist just proposed a shared speed limit for AI labs.

Jakub Pachocki argues developers should agree common limits, based on perplexity and other measures, a score of how well a model predicts the next token. He published OpenAI's own numbers to start the conversation.

→ GPT-4 sat at about 0.91 and was good at chain-of-thought reasoning; now that losses are below 0.8, OpenAI says it has seen transformative capabilities in cybersecurity and mathematics
→ Labs would commit not to cross the limits until our ability to understand and monitor AI reaches a concrete milestone; no cap is set yet
→ TechCrunch reports Sam Altman called it "the most important thing OpenAI has published in a while"; Dario Amodei's plan to "pace the frontier" was seemingly endorsed by Altman and Elon Musk

Would rival AI labs ever agree on a common brake?

Source: OpenAI, "Perplexity and Intelligence", Nov 22, 2026; TechCrunch, "OpenAI’s chief scientist has thoughts on how to limit AI development", Nov 22, 2026.
